Conversation
kon-ver-SAY-shun
noun
From the Latin conversari, “to turn oneself about, to dwell, to live among” (con- + versari, “to be turned”); hence one’s whole manner of living and dealing among men. The narrowing to mere talk is a later drift; the KJV means conduct.

Biblical Definition

Conversation in the Authorized Version is not talk. It is a man’s whole manner of life — his conduct, his walk, his behaviour, the sum of how he lives and deals among men. The Latin behind it means to turn oneself about among others, to dwell, to have one’s daily converse; and so the KJV can command a thing no one could command of mere speech: “let your conversation be as it becometh the gospel of Christ” (Php 1:27) — let your living match the gospel. Peter grounds it in the character of God: “as he which hath called you is holy, so be ye holy in all manner of conversation” (1Pe 1:15) — not holy in your talk merely, but in every department of your conduct. Paul can speak of his former conduct in the same word: “ye have heard of my conversation in time past in the Jews’ religion, how that beyond measure I persecuted the church of God” (Gal 1:13). That was no manner of speaking; it was a manner of life spent in fury against the saints. And the believer’s true home shapes the whole of it: “our conversation is in heaven; from whence also we look for the Saviour” (Php 3:20) — our citizenship, our commonwealth, the polity to which our lives belong, is above. Here is sanctification in one old word. A holy conversation is not smooth religious speech but a life visibly conformed to Christ, ordered by heaven’s laws while the feet still tread the earth. Men shall know the tree by more than its leaves; they shall know it by its walk.

Webster 1828 Definition

One’s whole manner of life and conduct among men — not, as now, mere talk.

CONVERSATION, general course of manners; behaviour; deportment; manner of living.

From Latin conversari, “to live among, to have dealings with.”

The narrowing to spoken discourse is a later and lesser sense of the word.

Paul’s conversation in time past was persecuting the church (Gal 1:13).

The believer’s conversation is in heaven, whence he looks for Christ (Php 3:20).

Key Scripture

Php 1:27 — "Only let your conversation be as it becometh the gospel of Christ: that whether I come and see you, or else be absent, I may hear of your affairs, that ye stand fast in one spirit, with one mind striving together for the faith of the gospel;"

1Pe 1:15 — "But as he which hath called you is holy, so be ye holy in all manner of conversation;"

Gal 1:13 — "For ye have heard of my conversation in time past in the Jews' religion, how that beyond measure I persecuted the church of God, and wasted it:"

Php 3:20 — "For our conversation is in heaven; from whence also we look for the Saviour, the Lord Jesus Christ:"

Modern Corruption

An old word for conduct; it recovers that holiness is a manner of life, not a manner of speech.

expand to see more

The honest drift here has cost the church dearly, for it has hidden a command in plain sight. When Peter says, “be ye holy in all manner of conversation,” the modern reader hears an exhortation to clean talk — no coarse jesting, no gossip — and while that is true and good, it is a fraction of the meaning. The word reaches the whole of a man’s conduct: his business, his marriage, his temper, his use of money and of time, his walk in the dark where no man sees. To collapse “conversation” into speech is to let nine-tenths of the command slip, and to imagine a man may be holy in his mouth while his life goes unreformed.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that the gospel commands a life. “Let your conversation be as it becometh the gospel of Christ” — the good news is to be adorned not by eloquence but by conduct, a walk that fits the doctrine. This is the doctrine of sanctification pressed into a single word: the called are to be holy in all manner of their living, because the God who called them is holy. And the spring of it is heavenly citizenship. The believer’s conversation is in heaven; his life is governed by the laws of a country he has not yet seen, and it is by that strange, upward-ordered walk that the world takes knowledge of him.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

The word means one’s whole manner of life and conduct — not merely speech.

expand to see more

Conversation — Latin conversari, “to live among.”

It means the whole course of one’s conduct and deportment.

The KJV never uses it for mere talk, but for manner of life.

Holiness is required in all manner of conversation (1Pe 1:15).

The saint’s conversation, his citizenship, is in heaven (Php 3:20).

Usage

"Conversation in the KJV is conduct: “be ye holy in all manner of conversation.”"

"Paul’s conversation in time past was persecuting the church — a life, not a speech."

"Our conversation is in heaven: the whole walk is ordered by a country above."
